text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cyprus is a volcano ready to explode if there is no solution soon, outgoing U.N. chief warns.
- Sharp words are exchanged between MPs during crime debate.
- Mum-to-be Zoi Efstathiou has six of 11 embryos removed. "I felt like I was carrying a football team," she said.
- Turks are furious at European Court's "political" ruling -- the government plays down the implications of the case.
- Bomb explodes outside Iranian businessman's Nicosia house.
- Man jailed for life is making threats against the former deputy police chief.
- The government makes a commitment in Brussels to deregulate interest rates without asking anyone.
- Non-existent industrial policy was revealed during a meeting of industrialists with the government.
- Accusations that police covered up for criminals were exchanged by MPs during a heated parliamentary debate.
- Commerce minister tells industrialists to forget about getting export subsidies from the government.
- Showdown in parliament between communist Akel and right-wing Disy over police's alleged involvement in organised crime.
- The United Nations repeats call for confidence building measures between the two sides in Cyprus.
